rationale: Requests the scope control for the identity finding: the same call, same cluster and same re-synchronization, but with the caller's entry replicated so that the following leader adopts it. The question's registered discriminator asks exactly this, and the local run shows the expectation (Ok is truthful once the entry is adopted), which bounds the defect to entries that never reached a quorum.

scope.description: Scope control for the identity case: the same completion endpoint and the same re-synchronization, but with the caller's entry replicated to a quorum and adopted by the following leader.
assumptions: 3 nodes, majority quorum, in-process delivery under harness control
node 1's own entry is accepted by both followers while their receipts are dropped, so node 1 cannot decide
the two calls are judged by comparing the reported index against the entry actually decided there
excluded: how often the unadopted variant occurs in a deployment

experiment.prefix: Same construction and transport as the executed revision (three real OmniPaxos instances over MemoryStorage warmed by omnipaxos_runtime actors from spawn_actor with a harness-local tokio-backed AsyncRuntime impl; a pump task per node into a shared queue plus one delivery task that drops messages whose sender or receiver is isolated and, in the new case, messages of a listed (sender, receiver) pair). Case `append_notify_ok_for_entry_overwritten_at_that_index`: node 1 is isolated in both directions, accepts its own entry at index 1, node 2 takes over with an empty log and decides index 1 with its own entry, node 1 re-synchronizes and its call resolves Ok(1) while the entry there is node 2's. New case `ok_is_truthful_when_the_entry_is_adopted`: node 1 is leader; the pair (2,1) and (3,1) are dropped so both followers accept node 1's entry but node 1 never learns it (asserted a_decided_before == 0); node 2 takes over (`try_become_leader`), adopts the followers' log containing node 1's entry and decides index 1; the pairs are then released and node 1 is asked to reconnect, after which its call must resolve Ok(idx) with node 1's own entry at that index. RuntimeConfig: tick_period 2000ms, egress_period 1ms, append_notify_timeout 30s.
experiment.revision_reason: Adds one case (`ok_is_truthful_when_the_entry_is_adopted`) and one transport facility (a list of (sender, receiver) pairs whose messages are dropped); the existing case and its assertions are unchanged. The new case is the scope control for the windowed finding: node 1 accepts its own entry at index 1 while *both* followers' receipts are dropped, so node 1 stays at decided 0 with its call pending although a quorum accepted the entry; node 2 then takes over, adopts the followers' log (which contains node 1's entry), decides index 1, and node 1 re-synchronizes. The expectation from the adoption path (prepare-phase Promise log_sync / take_max_promise_sync) is that Ok(1) is then truthful, i.e. the entry at index 1 is node 1's own. Locally both cases pass in 4.0s: the new case emits adopted_entry_resolution {a_decided_before: 0, a_decided_idx: 1, a_entry_at_index_1_is_own: true, b_decided_idx: 1, resolution: "Ok(1)"} beside the windowed case's overwritten_index_resolution {..., a_entry_at_index_1_is_own: false, ..., resolution: "Ok(1)"}.
